title: Distribució anual de les causes d'avaria dels mòbils (MobiFix)

problem.statement: ¿Cuál es la causa de avería de los móviles en cada año y cómo cambia año tras año la distribución de causas?
domain_examples: causes d'avaria de mòbils per any
tipus d'incidència per mes en un servei

values.derivation: count of repairs per (year, cause) / count of repairs in that year

encodings.note: one scale for all cells (0-40 %); value also printed in each cell
outline around the row the title is about

derived_data: share = count per (year, cause) / count in that year * 100
n per year as a separate bar strip on its own scale from zero
solution.ordering: rows by total descending, Altres and Desconegut last and separated; columns chronological, Tot column after a gap

color.note: blue family of poblacio_mobils_uk.png extended (L* 96->42); n bars in coral #DE9483 (#EDBBAE hatched for small n); slate #5B6573 outline; text #333333 on #FBFAF7; cell text white or #333 by WCAG contrast

text.title: takeaway
annotations: small-n years flagged with asterisk and hatched bar

rejected_alternatives.reason: 8 categories; only the bottom layer has a baseline, so shares of the middle causes cannot be compared year to year; the seed default fits <=5 categories
same baseline problem: only Pantalla (bottom) and the top segment are comparable
ribbon width mixes volume and share, ~62 crossing ribbons, no common baseline; year to year comparison impossible
8 lines (>7) with overlapping values at 0-15 %; direct labels would collide
8 panels with tiny n in several years; heatmap shows the same 64 values with exact numbers in one view

library_notes.matplotlib: Rectangle per cell + text; bar strip in a shared-x axis above

rationale: Position carries both keys exactly and each column sums to 100 %, so the reader compares a year's cause distribution by scanning a column and a cause's trend by scanning a row. Printed values give the precision a luminance ramp cannot, and the n strip keeps volume apart from share. Chosen over the stored stacked area because 8 categories exceed its scale.
